newsitem.title: UK: Hunting sees small yr profit, 6p final div.
newsitem.headline: Hunting sees small yr profit, 6p final div.

text.p: Hunting Plc, the aviation, defence and oil group which slumped to a first half loss of 14.2 million in the first half, said it expected to move to a small profit in the full-year results.

In its results statement on Tuesday Hunting said it would not be paying a half-year dividend but added that if conditions improve in the second half, as expected, it forsees a 6 pence final dividend payout.
The interim results were hit by 40.5 million stg of provisions for problems in the aviation unit.
Hunting's interim statement said the first six months had been difficult, but it added that "the outlook for the remainder of 1996 and 1997 is promising."
If this forecast proves accurate it expects to be able to maintain last year's final dividend of six pence this year.

The aviation provisions which hit Hunting's first-half result comprised 30 million stg for losses on its contract to fit interiors for Bombardier's Dash-8 and 10.5 million stg to write off investment in the BAe Jetstream 41 turboprop.
Ken Miller, chief executive, said he did not expect any further negative impact from the two problems.
Miller said the problems in aviation were being resolved. He also reported "excellent" prospects for the oil division and added that the defence order book was strong.

Looking at a divisional breakdown, the group is currently reviewing the aviation unit's management controls and systems. It has commissioned an independent report from Ernst and Young which will be finalised by the close of September.

Aviation made a loss after the exceptionals of 35.7 million stg, down from a 3.3 million stg profit. Defence profits were 7.4 million stg versus 7.2 million stg and the oil division's operating profits leapt 36 percent to 11.6 million stg.
Oil also contributed a one-off profit of seven million stg from sale of a construction business.
